# Functionality and Quality-Adjusted Optimization Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `executing`
- Updated: `2026-10-22T01:06:49Z`

## Objective

Improve the responsiveness, reliability, resource efficiency and demonstrated user outcomes of implemented features while preserving current authorization, immutable evidence and supported runtime boundaries. Planning only; implementation requires explicit approval.

## Discovery

Static review confirms substantial implemented shared workflows and deterministic tests, but current performance and user/model qualification are not established. Prioritize bounded navigation/read projections, task observation and cleanup, and quality-preserving Context allocation improvements; use existing roadmap owners for unfinished qualifications. No optimization or product behavior was changed during this assessment.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: Planning artifact changes are inert, but the proposed implementation crosses authorized read projections, runtime task lifecycle, model/resource handling and untrusted Context data. Existing controls remain acceptance constraints.
- Protected assets:
  - Workspace and organization data isolation
  - Immutable asset/release and dataset lineage
  - Source content, embeddings and model references
  - Runtime resource ownership and sanitized evidence
- Trust boundaries:
  - Renderer/API/IPC to authorized application read models
  - Task observations to host-owned runtime lifecycle
  - Saved context bytes to private managed-runtime validation
  - Controlled measurements to read-only review evidence
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - A fast summary crosses workspace or organization boundaries
  - Cancellation or navigation loses terminal cleanup or permits duplicate work
  - Allocation optimization skips digest, vector or citation validation
  - A benchmark reports no-op timing or silently omits failures
  - Telemetry retains protected content or implicit model/network authority
- Controls:
  - Authoritative actor/workspace context and scoped read ports
  - Idempotent lifecycle cleanup independent of UI observation where supported
  - Exact integrity/schema/lineage validation before query results
  - Bounded counts, concurrency, retries, memory and sanitized projections
  - No persistent content/model cache or new retrieval policy without a separate decision
- Verification:
  - Cross-workspace/organization, stale-revision and unauthorized-read denial tests
  - Fake-clock task observation plus real host terminal/cancel/shutdown failure paths
  - Corrupt package/vector/citation denial under optimized Context processing
  - Production-path workload assertions and controlled before/after memory/latency evidence
  - Existing security remediation evidence and manual reviews remain separately owned
- Residual risks:
  - Physical model, dedicated hardware, assistive-technology and managed-service qualification was not run
  - Host-owned cleanup and memory behavior must be measured before claiming reliability or performance gains
  - Unfinished security and legacy qualification roadmaps may block deployment qualification

### Constraints

- The user requested assessment and a roadmap only. No implementation, roadmap approval, completion evidence or reviewer identity is inferred.
- Use existing accepted contracts, application ports, shared UI and host ownership. No new deployment topology, streaming protocol, vector index, model provider or cache-retention policy is selected.
- All new numerical targets are proposals for roadmap approval, not observed baselines or production service-level commitments. Measure unchanged baseline and candidate on the same named controlled environment.
- Existing six asset/system p95 budgets remain authoritative. Owned probes must call real production paths and assert results rather than timing no-op doubles.
- The current all-suite report is failed: standard Node has 3030 passes, 36 failures and 1 skip; standard Vitest has 407 passes, E2E Node has 91 passes and 2 skips, and E2E Vitest has 3 passes. Triage unrelated failures separately before final qualification; these counts alone do not establish product defects.
- Security remediation owns renderer-editable model deletion roots, workspace staging/raw-key fallback, read/list registration mutations, Git adoption and helper path integrity. Optimize only after applicable controls are reconciled; never restore an insecure fallback for performance.
- Preserve legacy roadmap approvals and pending qualification. New evidence must be current and explicitly linked; no old pass becomes a control-plane receipt.

## Increment 1: Responsive workspace navigation and composition

- Id: `responsive-workspace-browse`
- Status: `implemented-pending-qualification`
- Dependencies: None

Make Home, feature summaries and Add element useful at representative catalog scale without transferring or re-reading entire collections for counts or one candidate page.

### Work packages

- **Restore demonstrated asset/workspace journey correctness before tuning** (`functional-contract-and-draft-replay`): Replay R62,R63,R64,R69,R70,R71,R72,R73,R75,R76,R78,R82,R88 against real typed clients/transports. Repair reproduced exact-version, malformed input, relationship/route parity, safe summary and Composer structure issues before counting a faster journey as success.
- **Own representative production-path probes** (`production-probes-and-baseline`): Extend the existing qualification harness with reproducible fixtures and real Catalog, Studio, resolver, build, preview and handoff paths; capture unchanged baseline before selecting repairs.
- **Bound dashboard summary reads** (`bounded-summary-projections`): Use application-owned authorized summary projections and shared clients rather than renderer full-list aggregation; preserve exact existing counting and unavailable semantics.
- **Reduce Composer candidate amplification** (`composer-candidate-efficiency`): Measure and bound exact-detail reads, compatibility filtering and cursor traversal; reduce redundant reads or use an adapter batch seam without exposing incompatible assets or skipping exact-version checks.
- **Verify navigation and composition outcomes** (`browse-journey-evidence`): Prove browse/search/add/save/reopen with current JSON evidence, keyboard and narrow layout behavior, and before/after workload results.

### Deliverables

- Repository-owned trusted production probe set using existing performance runner
- Baseline and candidate latency, I/O count and response-byte reports with source/environment identities
- Scoped summary use case/port/contract with API/IPC parity if needed
- Bounded Composer candidate path and focused regressions
- Updated architecture, owning README/context and qualification instructions
- Current replay and disposition of13 transferred functional findings, with focused contract/draft regressions before performance tuning

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transferred-asset-functional-rows`: All13 transferred asset/composition/workspace rows are replayed against the current source and classified with exact regression evidence or an explicit stale/deferred reason. Prove requested immutable versions, safe malformed-ref rejection, valid relationship and route/body contracts, non-shadowed projection routes, safe authoring summary/list shapes, current active-workspace recovery and structure-preserving subtree removal. Route admission remains finite, exact, authenticated and resource-authorized; unauthorized/unknown variants remain denied. No closure is inferred from the scanner report. | local | passed (review) |
| `owned-performance-probes`: All six configured operation/workload pairs have repository-owned probes that assert real outputs and negative failures. Record five warmups and at least thirty measured iterations on the same named environment; a no-op, mock-only or wrong-workload pass is rejected. | local | passed (test) |
| `summary-cost-and-truth`: For a fixture of 1000 active systems, 10000 releases, 10000 model records and 10000 custom-asset records, desktop/thin summary values exactly match the reference reducer. Proposed target: one bounded summary request per page and no transfer of full release locks or model/asset catalogs solely for counts; one unrelated metric failure does not hide already available independent metrics. | local | passed (review) |
| `composer-search-cost`: For 1000 authorized candidate definitions with sparse compatible matches and page size 25, candidate pages have no duplicates/skipped matches/repeated cursor loops; collect exact detail-read counts and payload bytes. Proposed target: at least 50 percent fewer detail-store round trips than unchanged baseline for the same complete compatible results; if no amplification exists, document the measured result instead of adding a speculative cache. | local | passed (review) |
| `browse-performance-qualified`: All six existing p95 budgets pass with exact declared workloads: browse200ms, validate350ms, resolve150ms, build2500ms, preview750ms and handoff500ms. Proposed page-level target: summary and first compatible candidate page each usable within p95 1000ms on the named reference desktop and managed-server/thin-client profiles, excluding deliberate network impairment. | controlled-environment | pending (test) |
| `browse-journey-preserved`: Search, Add element, selected exact detail, add/place, undo/redo, preview, save and reopen remain correct in both hosts; keyboard, focus restoration and 320 CSS-pixel reflow retain access to all controls. | local | passed (review) |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: Refresh the threat/control delta, prove isolation, failure bounds and non-disclosure for this increment, and preserve a rollback at least as secure as the forward path. Coordinate with the security remediation owner rather than duplicating its controls. | local | passed (review) |

### Verification

- While chunks remain, run dashboard reducer/client tests, Composer catalog/use-case tests, exact-version and cursor denial tests, and focused shared UI tests only.
- Measure counts/bytes with deterministic fixtures independently of timing; then run existing asset-system:performance against real production probes on controlled hardware.
- Run docs:check, architecture:check, agent-support:check when affected, and affected builds after the completed increment. Reserve test:all until every increment is implemented.
- Do not claim controlled performance from ordinary unit-test duration or a shared workstation visual run.

### Rollback

Revert the summary/candidate optimization as one slice while retaining fixture reports and isolation regressions. Restore the prior bounded authorized read path, never a raw-key fallback or removed security control. No persisted record migration is planned.

### Excluded

- Public marketplace, generalized search service or new deployment topology
- Cross-user or persistent content caching
- Security-owned read/list registration side effects
- Changing accepted Catalog/Studio/build performance budgets to accommodate a failure

## Increment 2: Efficient and reliable background task journeys

- Id: `efficient-reliable-task-journeys`
- Status: `implemented-pending-qualification`
- Dependencies: `responsive-workspace-browse`

Make downloads, preparation, Context generation, training and image generation remain understandable and release resources correctly when users navigate, disconnect, cancel or encounter a failure, while reducing idle polling.

### Work packages

- **Restore supported runtime/data paths before optimizing their observers** (`runtime-transport-and-result-replay`): Replay R55,R56,R58,R59,R61,R65,R67,R80,R83,R84,R85,R86. Verify API/preload/client parity, live readiness, workspace propagation, safe training materialization and generated-output identity, log freshness and logger failure containment. Unsupported model publishing is rejected before task dispatch.
- **Measure actual observer fan-out** (`task-observation-baseline`): Inventory page and shell observers, active/idle requests, duplicate notifications and terminal lifecycle ownership; use fake clocks and real host fakes to distinguish potential risks from observed failures.
- **Share bounded task observation** (`bounded-shared-observation`): Use an internal workspace-scoped single-flight observation layer over existing APIs, adaptive idle/error backoff and immediate refresh after explicit actions; preserve useful progress and truthful failures without new public streaming.
- **Prove terminal cleanup and recoverability** (`terminal-lifecycle-and-recovery`): Use existing host/runtime seams for idempotent terminal cleanup and task rediscovery; UI polling must not be the only release mechanism. Preserve cancellation and compensate failures without duplicate finalization.
- **Qualify active, idle and interrupted journeys** (`cross-feature-task-validation`): Demonstrate coherent task state and one terminal notification through leave/reopen, workspace switch, cancel, timeout, retry and host shutdown across supported task types.

### Deliverables

- Measured observer/lifecycle inventory
- Shared bounded polling/observation helper with deterministic clock tests
- Host-owned terminal cleanup and task recovery improvements where the baseline demonstrates gaps
- Focused desktop/thin task journey regressions and sanitized diagnostics
- Updated runtime, notifications and affected feature guidance
- Current replay and disposition of12 transferred functional findings, including explicit unsupported publishing rather than a speculative new worker

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transferred-runtime-functional-rows`: All12 transferred runtime/data/generation rows receive current contract-to-host replay and an evidence-backed fix or explicit unsupported/stale/deferred disposition. Preserve default-denied route policy and add only finite supported operation templates with authentication/resource authorization and negative variants. Logger normalization/serialization failure cannot break owning work, resource polls cannot consume log freshness, model publish cannot dispatch an unsupported task, dataset paths are privately materialized, image start/read/cancel carry workspace context and finalization is retry-safe. No unsupported provider capability or global fallback is introduced. | local | passed (test) |
| `idle-observer-budget`: Record unchanged and candidate idle request counts for ten minutes with one selected workspace. Proposed target: at least 80 percent fewer idle task-status requests than fixed1500ms bridges, at most one in-flight request per observer family/workspace, bounded terminal-ID retention, and no hidden-window polling that is unnecessary for cleanup. | local | passed (test) |
| `active-progress-budget`: Under a local healthy test transport, active task progress and terminal state appear within two seconds at p95; explicit start/cancel/refresh invalidates idle backoff immediately. Navigation/reopen and workspace changes never publish stale or cross-workspace state. Separate transport delay from UI delay. | local | passed (test) |
| `terminal-cleanup-independent`: A task that completes, fails, is cancelled or times out releases owned power/staging/process resources exactly once even when no feature page polls it; worker/host shutdown denies new work and reconciles existing records. Demonstrate this per supported lifecycle path; a TODO alone is not failure evidence. | local | passed (test) |

Unsupported cancel/retry remains clearly unavailable. | local | passed (test) |

| `security-impact-reviewed`: Refresh the threat/control delta, prove isolation, failure bounds and non-disclosure for this increment, and preserve a rollback at least as secure as the forward path. - Use focused fake-clock ModelDownloadNotificationBridge, ContextStudio and training/image-generation observer tests while iterating.
- Add terminal-with-no-UI, adapter-failure, duplicate-terminal, cross-workspace and bounded-retention tests at the lifecycle owner.
- Run applicable host lifecycle integration, renderer tests and changed builds at increment completion; keep cancellation that is unimplemented explicitly unsupported.
- Coordinate with security medium-runtime-and-process-hardening and the fresh security residual roadmap; do not parallelize changes to the same ownership/bounds path.

### Rollback

Revert observation scheduling/UI changes independently from host cleanup controls. Retain security/lifecycle fixes and regressions; restore only the previous bounded observer through the same authorized APIs. Never roll back to cleanup that depends solely on an open UI.

### Excluded

- WebSocket/SSE/public push protocol or new runtime topology
- New cancellation/retry promises for unsupported conversational runtime paths
- Security-owned authorization, staging and read/list registration remediation
- Provider-specific retry or automatic spend policies

## Increment 3: Quality-preserving Context and RAG efficiency

- Id: `quality-preserving-context-efficiency`
- Status: `implemented-pending-qualification`
- Dependencies: `efficient-reliable-task-journeys`

Reduce measured query allocation and repeated work in the existing portable LanceDB/Context workflow while preserving exact validation, citations and retrieval correctness.

### Work packages

- **Profile complete Context operations** (`rag-stage-baseline`): Measure retrieve/hash/materialize/table validation/model load/embed/search/cleanup separately, plus peak RSS, at 1000/10000/100000 chunks within existing package bounds.
- **Bound validation and query allocations** (`bounded-validation-allocation`): Use bounded Arrow iteration and minimal validated metadata rather than materializing a second full Python vector/text object graph, while checking every required vector/citation/schema invariant before returning results.
- **Protect retrieval and generation quality** (`quality-and-determinism-oracle`): Create a synthetic labeled corpus and query/citation oracle, retain exact search and tie semantics, test cleaning/chunking/source lineage, and retain all failed attempts in measurement evidence.
- **Compare exact baseline and optimized candidates** (`context-candidate-qualification`): Run current candidate against unchanged environment/model/corpus and report p50/p95, RSS, quality, failed/timeout/cancelled counts and bytes; choose further optimizations only from measured dominant stages.

### Deliverables

- Sanitized stage-level timing and peak-memory probe with versioned corpus/model/environment identities
- Bounded validation/query implementation only where profiling supports it
- Synthetic retrieval/citation/chunking quality oracle
- Before/after quality-adjusted cost/latency/memory report
- Updated Context threat model, architecture, tests and profile evidence

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `context-stage-baseline`: Capture cold and repeated query timings, stage durations, peak RSS and cleanup results at1000/10000/100000 chunks with declared384-dimensional embeddings where package bounds permit. Record unavailable workloads explicitly, not as passes; distinguish OS file-cache warmth from model reuse. | local | passed (test) |
| `context-allocation-target`: Proposed target: at10000 and100000 chunks, reduce incremental query peak RSS by at least25 percent against unchanged baseline without increasing p95 latency by more than5 percent, or demonstrate that the measured baseline already meets an explicitly approved environment budget. Keep source and package ceilings unchanged. | local | passed (test) |
| `context-quality-invariant`: For deterministic embeddings, top-k identities/order, scores within the fixed numerical tolerance and exact citations match unchanged exact-search results. For separately authorized local embedding runs, proposed recall@5 is at least0.90 on the labeled synthetic corpus with no regression greater than0.02; invalid/cross-workspace citations remain zero. Quality failures cannot be offset by a cheaper/faster result. | local | passed (test) |
| `context-integrity-and-cancel`: Every archive/table/vector/citation/digest denial remains enforced; cancellation and failure remove private materialization and produce sanitized bounded state. No optimization bypasses full required validation, downloads a model, retains query/source content or introduces a cross-request cache. | local | passed (test) |
| `context-runtime-qualified`: Representative CPU and sufficient accelerator profiles report actual local model identity, warm/cold p95, RSS, retrieval quality and cleanup; observed results remain distinct from deterministic conformance and from production guarantees. | controlled-environment | pending (test) |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: Refresh the threat/control delta, prove isolation, failure bounds and non-disclosure for this increment, and preserve a rollback at least as secure as the forward path. Coordinate with the security remediation owner rather than duplicating its controls. | local | passed (review) |

### Verification

- Run focused Context application/worker tests with injected deterministic embeddings; add bounded Arrow iteration, malformed vector/citation, cancellation and memory-accounting assertions.
- Use controlled isolated subprocess RSS measurements and existing managed runtime boundaries; do not infer memory wins from object-count assertions alone.
- Do not enable approximate indexing or a persistent extracted-package/model cache to meet the target. If profiling shows such a change is necessary, stop for a separate cache/retention/trust or retrieval-quality decision with concrete evidence.
- After the whole increment, run affected Context lifecycle integrations, policy/docs/architecture gates and host builds; reserve final test:all for the overall boundary.

### Rollback

Restore the exact validated query implementation and package format without changing stored artifacts. Retain integrity/citation regressions and measured baselines. Cleanup remains private, bounded and fail-closed; no cache migration is introduced.

### Excluded

- Approximate vector index, hybrid retrieval, rerankers or new embedding providers
- Persistent extracted-package cache, cross-request embedding-model cache or altered retention policy
- RAG integration into currently unsupported conversational retrieval/tools/memory
- Weakening exact package/schema/vector/citation validation for speed

| `accessibility-outcomes-qualified`: Automated packaged-desktop and thin-client UI checks verify keyboard traversal/activation, modal focus return, accessible names/roles/status semantics, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, computed contrast, status text independent of color and reduced motion on declared supported profiles. Critical automated exceptions, data loss or authority confusion block qualification. Retain actual DOM/semantic/visual evidence; unavailable checks remain pending. | controlled-environment | passed (test) |
| `model-quality-resource-outcomes`: For authorized installed-model trials, retain held-out task quality, invalid-output rate, retry count, accepted examples per minute, peak RAM/VRAM and elapsed time. A candidate requires no statistically material quality regression under a predeclared task metric/tolerance and at least20 percent better accepted-output throughput or demonstrated adherence to the approved resource budget. CPU/accelerator and constrained/unchecked modes are separate cohorts; unavailable runs remain pending. | controlled-environment | failed (external) |
| `full-current-qualification`: After every increment is implemented, triage the existing standard-Node failures without treating skips as passes, run test:all once plus relevant repository gates/builds, obtain separate-invocation current candidate review and complete the overall-validation work item. Every required controlled criterion must pass before final roadmap completion. | local | failed (test) |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: Refresh the threat/control delta, prove isolation, failure bounds and non-disclosure for this increment, and preserve a rollback at least as secure as the forward path. Coordinate with the security remediation owner rather than duplicating its controls. | local | passed (review) |

### Human scope handled offline

- User explicitly assigned human acceptance offline and requested agent-executable technical acceptance. Human portions of original instructions are superseded; no pass or closure is asserted. (`explicit-user-agent-only-acceptance`)
  - `user-task-outcome-targets`: Proposed study target: at least5 representative non-developer participants, at least4 of5 completing each assigned critical journey without facilitator intervention, zero critical data-loss/authority confusion, and median task ease at least5/7. Record sample size and limitations; do not infer population success or accessibility conformance from this small study. — offline user-owned; no test pass asserted.
  - Human portion of `accessibility-outcomes-qualified`: Manual screen-reader/operator acceptance and representative-participant evaluation are user-owned offline; automated accessibility and zero-data-loss/authority-confusion invariants remain technical requirements. — offline user-owned; technical criterion retained; no test pass asserted.

### Verification

- Use only the focused regressions for an actually observed gap during this increment; do not turn ordinary tests into timing gates or add speculative feature changes.
- Use existing controlled asset-experience, visual-composer, data-management, model-training and Context procedures with synthetic data, explicit operator authorization and installed runtimes.
- No provider calls, downloads, credentials, physical hardware qualification or participant study was performed during planning; these require their actual authorized controlled environment.
- At the final overall boundary, execute current all-suite and docs/architecture/agent-support/security-dependency/build gates as applicable, then independent technical review and final user approval. Pending external evidence blocks completion.

### Rollback

Withdraw or mark the candidate unqualified and return to the last secure qualified release. Revert only a measured UX repair that causes regression, retaining evidence and stronger security controls. Never declare a missing accessibility/model/provider qualification passed to preserve release timing.

### Excluded

- Inventing RPO/RTO, retention, encryption or availability objectives owned by operators
- New provider/model downloads or paid benchmark runs without authorization
- Implementing unapproved active-source or security successor roadmaps
- Broad UI redesign, new feature families, unsupported arbitrary code execution or production rollout
